title: Multi-Branch Decisions with if, else if, and else
learningObjectives: Explain sequential evaluation in an if/else if/else chain.
Write multi-branch decisions using if, else if, and else.
Predict which branch runs when multiple conditions could be true.
Order conditions to avoid broad rules blocking specific cases.
Identify missing coverage, unreachable branches, and condition-order mistakes.

understand.concept: A multi-branch decision checks conditions in sequence. The first true condition selects its branch and skips the remaining branches in the chain. An optional else handles the case where none of the earlier conditions is true.
understand.whyItMatters: Programs often need to choose one result from several categories. A single decision chain makes those alternatives clear and prevents multiple branches from running when only one outcome is intended.
understand.analogy: A service desk checks a queue of rules from top to bottom. When a rule matches, it directs the visitor to one service and the remaining rules are not checked.
understand.analogyLimit: Unlike a real queue, code evaluates Boolean expressions. A broad early condition can capture cases meant for a later, more specific condition, so rule order matters.

explain.narrative: Use if for the first condition, else if for additional alternatives, and optionally else for a fallback. Conditions are checked in order and the chain stops after the first true condition. This differs from separate if statements, where multiple blocks may execute. For numeric bands, order thresholds carefully and use clear boundaries. Validate invalid inputs separately when needed; an else branch should not silently treat invalid data as valid. Use braces and indentation to make branch ownership visible.

commonMistakes: Using separate if statements when only one outcome should be selected.
Putting a broad condition before a narrower condition, making later branches unreachable.
Forgetting a required fallback or using else to accept invalid input silently.
Using assignment instead of comparison in a condition.
Overlapping numeric ranges without tracing order.

guidedTask.title: Guided: Performance label
guidedTask.instructions: Select a label: 90+ is Excellent; 75+ is Good; 50+ is Pass; otherwise Retry. Print the label.
steps: Add else if branches for the next thresholds.
Use else for the remaining lower scores.

independentTask.title: Independent: Shipping category
independentTask.instructions: Categorize positive numeric package weight: up to 1 kg Light; over 1 and up to 5 Standard; over 5 and up to 15 Heavy; over 15 Oversize. Reject or separately handle zero, negative, or non-numeric input.
requirements: Validate input as numeric and positive first.
Use if/else if/else for four categories.
Make boundaries clear and avoid overlaps.
Produce one category for valid weights.

hints: The chain stops after the first true condition.
Put priority or narrow threshold rules before broad ones.
Descending numeric thresholds can prevent an early broad match.
Decide explicitly what the else branch represents.
Test exact boundaries and values just above/below them.
Separate if statements may run multiple times; a chain selects at most one branch.

questions.prompt: What happens after one condition is true in an if/else if chain?
options: That branch runs and the rest of the chain is skipped
questions.answer: That branch runs and the rest of the chain is skipped
questions.explanation: A chain selects the first matching branch and then exits the chain.

questions.prompt: Why should a broad threshold not come before a narrower threshold?
options: It may match first and make the narrower branch unreachable
It causes every branch to run
questions.answer: It may match first and make the narrower branch unreachable
questions.explanation: Conditions are checked in order, so an early broad condition can capture later cases.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of an optional else?
options: Handle cases when none of the earlier conditions match
Force all conditions to become true
questions.answer: Handle cases when none of the earlier conditions match
questions.explanation: Else is the fallback path for the chain.

questions.prompt: How do separate if statements differ from a single if/else if chain?
options: Separate if statements may each execute; a chain selects at most one branch
Separate if statements cannot contain comparisons
questions.answer: Separate if statements may each execute; a chain selects at most one branch
questions.explanation: Each independent if is checked separately, but a chain stops at the first true condition.

questions.prompt: What is a good way to test multi-branch decisions?
options: Test each outcome and values at numeric boundaries
questions.answer: Test each outcome and values at numeric boundaries
questions.explanation: Boundary tests reveal ordering and off-by-one errors; every branch should have coverage.
